name: threatlocker-mcp
description: Every ThreatLocker Portal API feature, plus the write operations the read-only tools lack and a cross-tenant offline store no other ThreatLocker tool has.

printing_press_client_profile.title: Client profile
printing_press_client_profile.description: Binds the MCP server to an existing tenant-gated Printing Press client profile.

threatlocker_api_key.title: ThreatLocker API key
threatlocker_api_key.description: Portal API key (ThreatLocker portal: Settings > API Keys), sent as the Authorization header on every call.

threatlocker_base_url.title: ThreatLocker API base URL
threatlocker_base_url.description: Base URL for the ThreatLocker API. Leave the prefilled default unless your account uses a different regional or self-hosted host.

threatlocker_org_id.title: Managed organization ID
threatlocker_org_id.description: Tenant GUID sent as ManagedOrganizationId (the --org flag overrides it). Most Portal API data calls answer 401/403 without it, so set it unless you pass --org on every call.

threatlocker_user_agent.title: User-Agent header
threatlocker_user_agent.description: Overrides the User-Agent the CLI sends on ThreatLocker requests. Leave blank to use the CLI's own built-in User-Agent.

threatlocker_mcp_read_only.title: Read-only MCP mode
threatlocker_mcp_read_only.description: Optional. Set to exactly 1 to expose only read-only tools and refuse any state-changing execute call. Leave blank to keep the write tools (they still need confirm).

threatlocker_no_local_data.title: Run without a local copy
threatlocker_no_local_data.description: Optional. Set to 1 to save no API data locally: sync and audit pull are refused, the response cache is off, and reads go to the API. Commands that read the local mirror still read what is already there. Leave blank to keep the local mirror.

threatlocker_mcp_http_token.title: MCP HTTP transport bearer token
threatlocker_mcp_http_token.description: Required only when running the MCP server with --transport http (a remote/hosted deployment). Callers must send a matching Authorization: Bearer header. Not needed for the default local stdio transport that Claude Desktop uses.
